name: ledger-source-of-truth
title: Feature ledger as source of truth: behaviours, parity, glossary, ios surface, validation
issue:
GOAL: make features.yaml (backend repo) a real SOURCE OF TRUTH for what each surface does and WHY, not just whether it exists, so a new surface (the iOS app is coming and will read this file) or a new agent can reproduce the product behaviour from the ledger plus the specs it points at. Today it records status per surface plus one-line notes and says it 'never restates the spec'. The user wants every BEHAVIOURAL CHOICE recorded and the file validated. Read features.yaml, tests/Qamooscheh.Api.Tests/Ledger/FeatureLedgerTests.cs, AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md first.

1. SCHEMA (extend, backwards compatible, enforced by the existing ledger test): (a) add an `ios` surface key to every feature (the iOS app does not exist yet: honest value is `not_yet` unless android is `n/a` for that feature, in which case `n/a`; backend-only/admin features `n/a`); update the header comment and test accordingly. (b) optional `behaviour:` list per feature: each item `{id (kebab, unique across the file), rule (one or two sentences, concrete, with the numbers), decided (YYYY-MM-DD), by (user|default|agent), applies (all or a list of surfaces), source (optional: spec section, PR or issue URL)}`. A behaviour is a user-visible or contract-visible rule a client must reproduce (XP amounts, cooldowns, thresholds, copy rules, ordering, defaults, privacy choices). Not implementation detail. (c) optional `parity:` list per feature for INTENTIONAL, user-accepted differences between surfaces: `{surface, difference, reason, accepted (YYYY-MM-DD)}` (these replace the ad-hoc 'accepted deviations' that today live only in orchestrator files). (d) optional top-level `glossary:` list `{term, meaning, code_note}` for product terminology. (e) extend FeatureLedgerTests to validate all of the above (unique ids, date formats, applies/surface names valid, declined needs reason as before, unknown keys rejected, parity surface must be a real surface, behaviour rule non-empty). Keep the existing 106 entries valid.

2. GLOSSARY seed: Parsle = a lesson in a unit/journey, also a custom grouping of lessons in Repack (a constructed Repack is a custom Parsle); Repack = the renamed Remix practice mode; Repack race = the timed ranked mode; 'Lesson complete' title removed entirely; cloze = fill-in-the-blank flashcard. code_note: code identifiers and API keys stay lesson / remix / cloze, only user-facing copy changed.

3. BACKFILL behaviours and parity for everything decided in this work (use `decided` 2026-10-14 unless a date is known; by: user unless noted). Find or create the right entry for each, keep ids stable, and cross-check every number against API_SPEC.md and the code on master so the ledger never contradicts it (if the spec and the decision differ, record the spec's value and flag it in your PR body):
- Usernames/friends (PR #46 etc.): handle 3-20 chars lowercase letters/digits/_/. ; unique case-insensitive; blocklist; existing users auto-backfilled and new accounts get user plus 8 digits (auto_assigned true); choosing the first handle or replacing an auto-assigned one is free and starts the clock; rename once per 30 days; the handle given up is held 30 days (only the previous owner can retake it); findable by default with opt-out; exact-match search only, 0 or 1 hit, rate limited 30/min shared with the availability check; display-name search removed; blocked pairs read as no relationship; Add is idempotent (Pending, never an error); relationship states none/request_sent/request_received/friends; identity is a Discord-style unique username plus a free display name (Name#1234 tags were rejected); pending-request lists withhold the username until accepted. Web parity: the friend profile page shows only data the backend returns (name, handle, friends-since, league rank/points if in cohort) and no streak/XP until a friend-stats endpoint exists; Android parity: View on a friend search hit only clears the search until an Android profile screen exists; search runs on submit not per keystroke (accepted 2026-10-14).
- Cloze flashcards (PR #47): XP 5 first attempt, 3 first retry, 1 second retry, no daily cap; per-word (card) daily cooldown on paid XP (user-accepted); regular mode accepts a one-letter typo, optional hardcore mode accepts none; multiple blanks ramp with difficulty; FSRS effect once per local day (attempt 1 good, 2 hard, 3+ again, clamped); results are stored (cloze_answer) with plausibility fields but no leaderboard/speed rejection yet; planned and NOT built: marathon mode runs to the learner's current position with a hint to unlock more units, records server-side with leaderboards global/regional (self-reported country)/weekly/friends per device class, speedrun clock pauses only for server latency, modal categories cloze cards vs full Parsle exercises ('Repack race').
- Repack organisation (agreed, NOT scheduled): one builder with source (Topics, Units/Parsles, Saved words, Due for review) x contents (exercise types incl. flashcards/fill-blank) x mode (relaxed, Race, hardcore toggle); entry points pre-fill; old URLs redirect; ranked races are fixed named presets, custom builds are practice-only.
- Stories as side paths (web #94): stories branch off the unit's last Parsle as junction spurs on the Journey road; a story is locked until the previous Parsle is passed (the library stays unlocked by unit); the main/first tag symbol sits alongside the title; the side a story hangs on is chosen by a stable hash per story; stories only (not other lesson kinds). Android not_yet.
- Open lessons survive redeploys (web #90, Android #60): an open lesson pins its content version, session plan and grader for its whole duration; deploy-triggered updates apply only between lessons. Recap (web #92): 1.9s eased fill with sound, burst, reveal, perfect chime, pass tick after the fill, Deep Dive panel with a 'Repack these topics' action; Android not_yet.
- CDN content cache (web #93, Android #61): each versioned CDN file downloaded once per version (cache-first, in-flight dedupe, errors never cached); pruning keeps the last N=3 versions of the live course plus the latest cached version of every other course; the version pinned by an open lesson is never pruned even beyond N. Planned, NOT built: auto-update course versions between lessons, remove the CourseUpdateBanner, backend keeps the last N versions and an expiry rule for very old mid-lesson sessions (age undecided). Needs from the backend (open): per-file sha256 in the course manifest and CDN retention for delta updates (web #82 stays open).
- Friend-request push (backend PR #49 and Android #63): category friend_requests defaults ON, stored server-side so nothing is sent when off, mirrored by a Settings switch; the payload carries the sender's DISPLAY NAME only, never the @username (user decision 2026-10-14, matches the pending-list rule); a repeat Add never re-notifies; blocked pairs never notify; Android only for now (ios/web tokens register but are skipped); a push token belongs to one account at a time; max 10 devices per user, the least recently seen is evicted; the feature is inert until a Firebase service account is configured; the Android permission ask goes through an in-app explainer shown in context (rule: permissions that fundamentally change how the app is used get an in-app explainer that asks, explains and nudges before the OS prompt). Read the PR branch for the final values; if it is unmerged, record them as the intended behaviour with source set to the PR.
- Onboarding (web): name step, then languages, then a tutorial walkthrough. Planned, NOT built (user-approved 2026-10-14): a username step after the name step: format validated instantly with no request, availability checked ~400ms after typing stops (debounced, stale requests cancelled, spinner then tick or reason), the server re-checks on submit, skip keeps the auto-assigned handle, choosing one starts the 30-day rename clock and the step says so. Contacts matching (hashed, opt-in, needs a backend endpoint) planned, NOT built.
- Parity/process decisions worth recording as behaviours or notes where a feature entry fits: streak animation (#52) and the art tickets are deferred pending art; Japanese embed removal (#84) deferred; the ra mistake hint shipped (#64) and a 'common mistakes' follow-up is wanted.

4. PROCESS (so it stays true): update the backend CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md ledger rules: any work that lands or changes a rule must add/update the feature's behaviour (and parity) entries in the same PR, with `decided` and `by`; the ledger is read first by new surfaces. Add a short docs/ledger.md describing the schema with a worked example and how a new surface (iOS) should consume it. Do not edit the web or Android repos; the orchestrator updates their CLAUDE.md files separately.

5. Keep the file readable: do not copy the spec's prose, only the rules/numbers a client must reproduce; one rule per behaviour item. Statuses for web/android must stay honest per the repos' main lines (check the recent merged PRs: web #89-#96, Android #59-#61 and #50 are merged; Android #62 and #63, web #97 and backend #49 are open and not yet in a main line, so record them as intended with the PR as source and leave their status exactly as the main line says).
acceptance: features.yaml has an ios key everywhere, optional behaviour/parity lists and a glossary, all validated by the ledger test
Every decision listed in the item is recorded with decided/by/applies and cross-checked against API_SPEC.md and master
CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md rules and docs/ledger.md explain how to keep it true and how iOS consumes it
dotnet build and the ledger test green locally
gate: approved by the user 2026-10-14 ('ensure all behavioural choices are documented in the ledger')
